subject: Orion Pilot: success gates, acceptance tests & go/no-go timeline
messages:

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Subject: Orion Pilot: success gates, acceptance tests & go/no-go timeline

Hi Alex / Procurement team,

Thanks again for the time earlier — excited to get our Orion pilot scoped. I attached a draft Mutual Action Plan (Orion_MAP_v1.pdf) and an initial acceptance-test catalog (orion-acceptance-tests-v1.xlsx). At a high level, this thread is to confirm the success criteria and the go/no-go gates so we can lock the pilot timeline.

Proposed high-level MAP items (please comment inline in the attachment):
- Pilot duration: 8 weeks (30-day evaluation + 30-day expansion / stress window)
- Primary success signals: 1) 95th pct latency < 450ms for 1k daily evals, 2) model match rate >= 88% against your adjudicated set, 3) token cost target met (< $0.003/token during steady-state)
- Exit gates (go): all three signals met on two consecutive weekly sample runs + no high-severity integration defects
- Exit gates (no-go): repeated regressions (>3 failed smoke runs in 2 weeks), data residency blockers unresolved, or procurement redlines that require Private deployment longer than 60 days

Acceptance-test highlights (see spreadsheet for full matrix):
- Smoke: end-to-end inference with sample V1 payloads (pass if success rate >= 98%)
- Concordance: 500 adjudicated prompts compared to your ground truth (pass if F1 >= 0.88)
- Load: sustained 200 QPS for 10 minutes with p95 latency < 500ms (pass/fail)
- Failover: region failover within configured 60s and no data loss

Ask from your side: can you confirm the three priority KPIs above and whether the 8-week cadence works? Also flag any contracts or compliance items that will block the go/no-go decision (SOC2 artifacts, data retention, or on-prem requirements).

Next step: if we get alignment by Thursday 6/3, I'll update the MAP and schedule a 30-minute kickoff to align owners and handoffs.

Attachments:
- Orion_MAP_v1.pdf (MAP draft, milestones & owners)
- orion-acceptance-tests-v1.xlsx (test matrix + sample datasets)

Thanks,
Soojin Lee

Subject: Re: Orion Pilot: success gates, acceptance tests & go/no-go timeline

Thanks, Soojin — useful starting point. A few clarifications from our engineering and procurement side: 

- Timeline: we generally prefer a 6-week proof + 4-week expansion, but we can be flexible if the MAP shows clear weekly checkpoints.
- KPIs: latency and concordance look fine, but procurement wants the cost target expressed as an expected monthly spend for a baseline volume (we estimated ~50k tokens/day for phase 1). Can you add an expected spend range?
- Compliance: SOC 2 evidence is required before any production rollout; for pilot we can accept an isolated demo dataset but we need a written data retention plan.

Also, two technical asks: 1) can you confirm whether KV cache warming is part of the smoke runs (we expect prefix patterns to matter), and 2) what quantization/variant will you serve for the pilot model?

I'll loop in our product lead if we need deeper infra answers. Assuming you can add the expected spend and the cache plan to the MAP, Thursday works to lock the kickoff.

Alex Park
Product Manager, Orion Health
alex.park@orionhealth.com

Soojin — drafted suggested edits for the MAP before sending back to Alex. Key recommended changes:

- Pilot cadence: propose 6 + 4 (6-week core eval, 4-week performance expansion). Makes procurement happy and compresses decision points into two main go/no-go reviews (end of week 3, end of week 6).
- Spend guidance: provide three bucket estimates (low/med/high) for 50k tokens/day baseline using current model variant; include a note that quantized variant reduces cost ~40% but may impact concordance by ~1.5 ppts.
- Exit gates: simplify to three deterministic checks to avoid ambiguity: 1) Pass smoke & concordance, 2) Latency p95 threshold met during two sustained runs, 3) No open Sev1/Sev2 integration defects assigned to our team and Orion owners.
- Acceptance tests: add a fast-retry failure mode test (simulate transient GPU OOM, ensure request retry succeeds within 120s) and an audit trace verification for 10 sample requests.

I'll attach the redline in the MAP PDFs. For the go/no-go language, recommend we make decisions binary — a single 'no-go' item triggers remediation plan and 2-week remediation window, then re-eval. If remediation fails, we recommend pausing and offering a credits extension for transparency.

If this looks good I can drop the updated MAP + spend buckets into Drive and send to Alex with the proposed kickoff slot (Thu 6/3 10:00am PT).

Marissa

Subject: RE: Orion Pilot: success gates, acceptance tests & go/no-go timeline

Alex — thanks for the quick read. We updated the MAP and acceptance catalog per your asks (Drive link below). High-level changes we made based on your notes and an internal redline: 

- Pilot cadence: 6-week core evaluation (midpoint checkpoint at W3) + 4-week expansion window for performance scaling.
- Spend estimate (50k tokens/day baseline): low ~$6k/mo, med ~$9k/mo, high ~$13k/mo (numbers include expected batching and cache benefits; spreadsheet shows per-test breakdown).
- Cache warming: included in smoke runs, and we added a short warmup protocol (50 synthetic prefixes run for 30m) before concordance runs.
- Model variants: pilot will run quantized-8 variant by default; we documented an A/B to non-quantized on a sampled subset to measure concordance delta.
- Go/no-go (final): go if (1) smoke & concordance pass, (2) p95 latency < 450ms during two sustained runs, (3) no open Sev1/Sev2 integration defects. No-go triggers remediation plan with a 2-week remediation window.

Attachments & links:
- Updated MAP (Orion_MAP_v1.pdf) — redline accepted and clean copy in Drive
